title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing the previous page). X is the Riemann sphere. G is the group of conformal and anticonformal automorphisms, and G+ = PGL2(C) is its conformal part. H is a compact (typically finite) subgroup of G with H+ = H ∩ G+. Spherical metrics on X correspond to positive Hermitian forms on V = C^2 up to scalars, i.e. to points of hyperbolic 3-space. Herm**(V)^H is the cone of H-invariant forms. The section asks when the H-invariant spherical metric fails to be unique, and parametrizes all of them.

Previous page. If H+ ≠ 1 fixes two points z, z', the invariant metrics are those invariant under the unique maximal compact torus T ≅ U(1) of the stabilizer C* of {z, z'}. They correspond 1-1 to T-orbits in X \ {z, z'}, i.e. to the circle that is the 'equator' for the poles z, z'.

This page treats H ≠ H+.

(a) H+ = 1, so H = {1, σ} with σ an anticonformal involution.
- (1) If σ has no fixed points (antipodal map), there is a unique σ-invariant spherical metric.
- (2) If X^σ ≠ ∅, σ is an inversion (reflection) in a circle C. A σ-invariant spherical metric is then the same as an unordered pair {x, σx} of σ-conjugate points, which serve as the poles. So any x with σx ≠ x defines one.
- Hyperbolically: the fixed set of a reflection is a totally geodesic plane bounded by C. Each point of that plane is the foot of a unique perpendicular geodesic, whose endpoints are x and σx.

(b) H+ ≠ 1. Let T be the unique maximal torus containing H+, and N = T·H. N is an extension of γ = Z/2 by T, and the anticonformal elements of N either fix or swap z, z'.
- The text first links 'fix' to trivial action of γ on T and 'swap' to t ↦ t^{-1}. The marginal note 'c'est l'inverse!' corrects this.
- Concretely, for z, z' = 0, ∞: σ(z) = a z̄ fixes 0 and ∞ and conjugates t to t^{-1}. σ(z) = b/z̄ (b real) swaps them and commutes with T.
- Tate cohomology. Trivial action: Ĥ^2(γ, T) = T/T^2 = 0 (U(1) is divisible), so the extension splits. Inversion action: Ĥ^2(γ, T) = T^γ/N(T) = {±1}/1 = Z/2.
- Case 1 (swap, trivial action): N ≅ T × γ, generated by T and an anticonformal involution σ interchanging z, z'. The text goes on to argue σ can be taken to be an inversion.
- The next page completes this. σ is only defined up to ε = −1 ∈ T, and {σ, εσ} = {z ↦ b/z̄, z ↦ −b/z̄} consists of one inversion and one antipodal map. The inversion's circle |z|^2 = b becomes the equator of the invariant metric.

Purpose: a case-by-case classification of finite groups of conformal/anticonformal symmetries of the sphere and their invariant round metrics. It is part of the 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' project of gluing surfaces from metrically standard pieces.
errors: The first attribution (elements fixing z, z' ↔ trivial action on T) is reversed. Grothendieck catches this himself in the margin ('c'est l'inverse!'): fixing z, z' gives t ↦ t^{-1}, swapping gives trivial action. The written 'Dans le 1er cas ... triviale' computation is therefore attached to the swap case, as the subsequent case 1) confirms.
'N ≅ T ⋊ γ (produit semi-direct)': in the swap case the action is trivial, so it is in fact a direct product. This is harmless.

In the inversion-action case Ĥ^2 = Z/2 is the abstract cohomology group. The extension actually realized inside G still splits: z ↦ a z̄ with |a| = 1 is an involution, giving O(2). The page does not draw this conclusion explicitly, but it is not an error.

ideas.what: Spherical metrics on CP^1 invariant under a compact group ↔ fixed points in hyperbolic 3-space (positive Hermitian forms mod scalars); non-uniqueness occurs exactly when the conformal part fixes two points
ideas.modern_name: Fixed-point sets of compact subgroups of Isom(H^3) acting on Herm^+(C^2)/R^+
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré, Klein; standard Kleinian group theory)

ideas.what: Dichotomy for anticonformal involutions: antipodal map (unique invariant metric) vs. inversion in a circle (invariant metrics parametrized by conjugate pairs {x, σx})
ideas.modern_name: Real structures on P^1: real-points-empty (quaternionic/antipodal) vs. reflection; invariant metrics ↔ points of the fixed hyperbolic plane

ideas.what: Use of Tate cohomology Ĥ^2(Z/2, U(1)) to decide splitting of the normalizer extension N of Z/2 by the circle T, depending on the action (trivial → 0, inversion → Z/2)
ideas.modern_name: Classification of extensions of Z/2 by U(1) (O(2) vs. U(1)×Z/2, Pin-type extensions)

ideas.what: The anticonformal lift σ commuting with T is defined up to ε = −1, and {σ, εσ} = {inversion, antipodism}
ideas.modern_name: z ↦ b/z̄ with b > 0 vs. b < 0

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely classical case analysis of invariant round metrics under finite groups of conformal/anticonformal maps of the sphere. Its only interest is as a building block of Grothendieck's 'conformal surgery' project, which is itself little documented; nothing on this page is new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'est un [-..-] Z/2Z par T' should read roughly 'est ext[ension] de Z/2Z par T'.

'Considérons le {+unique+} [-tore-] [-B..-] compact maximal' should read 'Considérons le {unique} tore compact maximal T'. 'unique' is inserted above, and the word after 'tore' is a corrected/overwritten word, likely 'compact'.
'(sous ${}_2T$ : Z/2Z)' is not parenthetical text. It is an underbrace label 'Z/2Z' written under _2T in the formula H^2(γ,T) ≃ T^σ/N_γ(T) ≃ _2T/0 ≃ Z/2Z.
'$\overset{\gamma=}{}\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$' is the notation γ = Z/2Z written above the Z/2Z in 'l'ext. N de Z/2Z par T'.
'Dans le 1er [?] cas, on peut [?] ...' is likely 'Dans le 1er cas, on trouve que l'ext. N de γ = Z/2Z par T est triviale'.
In a)2), 'i.e. [?] σ une inversion' is 'i.e. σ est une inversion'.
The superscript 'x)' after 'point' marks the inserted point x ('le choix d'un point x de X tel que σx ≠ x').
